evidence.quote: A VideoCardz source confirmed that one board partner already has RTX 50 Super GPUs on hand, but Nvidia has allegedly told the company that the products are on hold because of the price of 3GB GDDR7 memory chips.
evidence.one_line: An unnamed VideoCardz source said a board partner had RTX 50 Super GPUs on hand and Nvidia had allegedly put the products on hold because of 3GB GDDR7 chip prices.
evidence.speaker: Tom's Hardware, reporting a VideoCardz source

evidence.quote: This means that the AI GPU giant has already set an internal release date but is reportedly pushing it back because of memory pricing.
evidence.one_line: Tom's Hardware reported that Nvidia had set an internal RTX 50 Super release date and was reportedly pushing it back because of memory pricing.
evidence.speaker: Tom's Hardware

evidence.quote: The RTX 50 Super GPUs are rumored to have 3GB GDDR7 chips , which offers 50% more capacity than the 2GB found in current-gen RTX 50-series graphics cards.
evidence.one_line: The article said the rumored RTX 50 Super GPUs would use 3GB GDDR7 chips, 50% more capacity than the 2GB chips in current RTX 50-series cards.
evidence.speaker: Tom's Hardware

evidence.quote: According to the publication, the cards expected to be released soon include the RTX 5080 Super, RTX 5070 Ti Super, RTX 5070 Super, and RTX 5050 9GB.
evidence.one_line: The article reported that four cards were expected soon: RTX 5080 Super, RTX 5070 Ti Super, RTX 5070 Super, and RTX 5050 9GB.
evidence.speaker: Tom's Hardware, citing the publication
evidence.original_who: The publication cited by Tom's Hardware

evidence.quote: The first two will each receive 24GB of GDDR7 VRAM with a 256-bit bus width, while the RTX 5070 Super will have 18GB of VRAM with a 192-bit bus width.
evidence.one_line: The article reported that the RTX 5080 Super and RTX 5070 Ti Super would each have 24GB GDDR7 and a 256-bit bus, while the RTX 5070 Super would have 18GB and a 192-bit bus.
evidence.speaker: Tom's Hardware, citing the publication
evidence.original_who: The publication cited by Tom's Hardware

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, these chips cost twice or thrice as much as their 2GB variants, which will likely push the retail price of these cards beyond Nvidia’s envisioned MSRP.
evidence.one_line: The article said 3GB GDDR7 chips cost two to three times as much as 2GB variants and could push the cards' retail prices above Nvidia's envisioned MSRP.
evidence.speaker: Tom's Hardware

evidence.quote: Nvidia used to supply VRAM chips alongside GPU dies to its board partners, but it changed this policy in late 2025 as the memory chip crisis unfolded.
evidence.one_line: The article said Nvidia changed its policy in late 2025 and stopped supplying VRAM chips alongside GPU dies to board partners.
evidence.speaker: Tom's Hardware

evidence.quote: SK hynix, one of the big three memory chip manufacturers, even says that 2027 is set to be the “worst year” for the memory shortage and said that the crunch will last until 2030.
evidence.one_line: SK hynix said 2027 was set to be the worst year of the memory shortage and that the shortage would last until 2030.
evidence.speaker: Tom's Hardware, reporting SK hynix's remarks

evidence.quote: Even Nvidia, one of the biggest winners in the AI race, has been affected by the RAMpocalypse, with the company not announcing a new GPU at CES 2026 .
evidence.one_line: Nvidia did not announce a new GPU at CES 2026.
evidence.speaker: Tom's Hardware

evidence.quote: Its latest AI systems are now more expensive than ever, with memory accounting for 25% of the BOM, as costs have soared by nearly 500%.
evidence.one_line: The article said memory accounted for 25% of the bill of materials for Nvidia's latest AI systems and that costs had risen nearly 500%.
evidence.speaker: Tom's Hardware
